name: Metabase
description: Open source business intelligence and analytics platform. Create dashboards and explore data without writing SQL.
summary: Metabase is actively maintained with frequent patch releases across multiple supported versions. The latest stable release is v0.63.1 (OSS) / v1.63.1 (Enterprise), released on July 21, 2025 (https://github.com/metabase/metabase/releases/tag/v0.63.1). Multiple older branches (v0.58–v0.62) are receiving concurrent patch updates, indicating a strong LTS-style support policy. A v0.63.0-beta was also released on July 8, 2025, though it is not recommended for production use.

answers.What is the current license?: Open Source edition uses AGPL v3; Enterprise edition has a commercial license
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases across several version branches within July 2025
answers.Is there a cloud-hosted version availabl: Yes — Metabase Cloud (managed cloud) is available at metabase.com
answers.Does it support SSO and SAML authenticat: Yes — SSO and SAML are supported in the Enterprise edition
answers.What databases/data sources are supporte: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, MongoDB, Presto, Druid, Oracle, SparkSQL, and more (full list at metabase.com/docs)

alternatives.name: Redash
alternatives.review: Open source, query-focused, simpler feature set.

alternatives.name: Apache Superset
alternatives.review: Apache-licensed, rich visualisation library, steeper setup curve.

alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.review: Primarily metrics/time-series but increasingly used for general BI.

alternatives.name: Hex
alternatives.review: Close source, enterprise focus, AI Analytics Platform for your whole team

alternatives.name: Tableau
alternatives.review: Offers more advanced visualizations and enterprise features than Metabase, but is proprietary, expensive, and not self-hostable in the traditional sense.

alternatives.name: Lightdash
alternatives.review: Tightly integrates with dbt for a metrics-first approach which is more structured than Metabase, but requires a dbt project as a prerequisite.
